answer: Each agent ID must answer a live latency check: a beacon node broadcasts a fresh random seed every hour, and the ID has 400 ms to return a signed hash from a hardware attestation key on its own machine. We place probe servers in karst caves at different depths so round-trip timing reveals where a responder is located. A farm can't run fifty IDs off one box, because each key is fused to a separate crystal oscillator chip and responses from the same host collide in timing. Every fake needs its own device, roughly $80 plus power, so fifty fakes cost fifty devices.
